message.content:
Sure! Here are a few common appliances that can bake a chocolate cake, along with a quick note on how to use each one:

| Machine | How it works for a chocolate cake | Tips |
|---------|-----------------------------------|------|
| **Conventional oven** | The classic choice—just bake a batter in a cake pan at 350 °F (175 °C) for 25–35 min. | Use a spring‑form pan for easy release; line with parchment for extra safety. |
| **Microwave** | Great for a single‑serving “mug cake.” Mix batter in a mug and microwave 60–90 s. | Use a microwave‑safe mug; watch the cake so it doesn’t over‑bake. |
| **Slow cooker** | Place a greased cake pan in the slow cooker and cook on low for 2–3 h. | Cover the lid loosely to keep moisture in; check for doneness with a toothpick. |
| **Pressure cooker** | Similar to a slow cooker but faster—cook on low pressure for 30–45 min. | Use a cake pan that fits inside; keep the lid slightly ajar to avoid steam buildup. |
| **Bread machine (cake setting)** | Many bread machines have a “cake” mode. Pour batter into the basket and let it bake. | Use the machine’s cake setting; add a splash of milk or water to keep the batter from drying out. |
| **Air fryer** | Works well for small cakes or cupcakes—use a silicone cup or small pan. | Preheat to 320 °F (160 °C); cook 12–15 min, checking frequently. |

If you’re looking for a quick recipe that works in any of these machines, just let me know what ingredients you have on hand and I can pull up a suitable chocolate cake recipe for you!
